messages:
Anya: Nightly eval flagged a sudden failure cluster on summarization-promptset after the v41b weight merge. 30% drop on ROUGE-L for 08:00 run. Anyone else seeing this?
NightlyBot: automated: /evals/job/2026-03-19/3512349876 completed. regressions: summarization-promptset (ROUGE-L -30%), list-formatting spike. linked: https://ci/redwood/evals/3512349876
Ben: ugh. re-run artifacts? can you dump an example input + v40.2 vs v41b outputs?
Anya: pasted minimal repro below. note this is from the nightly artifact.
Anya: ```
INPUT: "Summarize the following meeting notes into bullets."
DOC: "Attendees: Alice, Bob. Discussed rollout. Action: deploy on Thu. Follow up: API tokens rotation."
V40.2: "- Attendees: Alice, Bob
- Discussed rollout
- Action: deploy on Thu
- Follow up: rotate API tokens"
V41b: "- Attendees: Alice, Bob
- Discussed roll ou t
- Action: deploy on Th
- Follow up: rotate API to kens"
```
Anya: weird token splits in middle of words (`roll ou t`, `to kens`).
Samir: that looks like a tokenizer merge change. v41b PR changed BPE merges and applied new byte fallback mapping. possible off-by-one in merge table import.
Cody: could also be KV-prefix mismatch: if tokenization changed, cache prefix alignment for streaming/rerank paths can corrupt continuation tokens and cause mid-word splits on generation.
Ben: steps: 1) confirm tokenizer vocab checksum between v40.2 and v41b. 2) run tokenization diff on failing inputs. 3) check runtime code that consumes token ids for KV cache.
Theo: quick checks I ran: vocab sha: v40.2=3a7f9b, v41b=3a7f9b (same) but merges file length differs (v40.2: 125k, v41b: 125k). however token->byte mapping for bytes >0x7f changed in one helper fn. suspect fallback table reorder.
Anya: good catch. can you paste the tokenizer diff? even a one-line reorder could explain this.
Theo: short diff: `byte_fallback = sorted(fallback.items())` -> `byte_fallback = list(fallback.items())`. previously stable sort ensured deterministic ordering; new code uses insertion order from YAML which differs across environments.
Samir: that matches. tokenizer nondeterminism -> different merge application -> subtoken boundaries differ -> generation continuum broken when using cached KV prefetched from earlier tokens.
Marta: ops: paused canary deploy to prod and dedicated pools. marking rollout hold. :warning:
Cody: next steps I can take: (a) re-run a deterministic tokenizer build and generate deterministic merges, (b) run a quantized inference run to see if quant path masks the effect, (c) add a short unit test in tokenizer CI to assert stable ordering. which should I start with?
Ben: start with (a) and (c) in parallel. quant run (b) as follow-up; could take longer.
Anya: can you also attach a short eval with `--no-cache` to check if the issue is only when KV caching is enabled?
Cody: yes. re-runs queued:
Cody: `./scripts/eval_run.sh --model v41b --promptset summarization-promptset --no-cache --seed 42`
Cody: queued `./scripts/eval_run.sh --model v41b --promptset summarization-promptset --with-cache` for comparison.
NightlyBot: re-run started: 3512350001 (no-cache), 3512350022 (with-cache). will post results.
Cody: local quicks: no-cache run looks fine (ROUGE ~ baseline). with-cache shows the same mid-token corruption. so confirmed: cache path interacts with tokenization nondeterminism.
Samir: probable root cause: non-deterministic byte fallback ordering when building merges yields token id mapping mismatch between when cache entries were created and when they are later used, leading to decoded token alignment errors.
Marta: recommend rollback to v40.2 in canary until fix is in. Ops approved rollback.
Anya: documenting: add regression note to internal eval tracker, tag `tokenizer`+`kv-cache`+`v41b`. PR link?
Samir: PR in flight: https://git/repo/pulls/6421 explaining fallback ordering fix. tests added.
Ben: after fix, we should run: deterministic tokenizer build, 3 full-nightly runs, and a small canary with dedicated pool. also add a quick integration test that runs a short seed generation with and without cache and assert byte-level equality.
Theo: I'll add the integration test. Marty/ops can resume canary once CI green.
Marta: noted. setting canary resume tentatively for 2026-03-21 02:00 UTC contingent on CI.
Anya: thanks everyone. good catch on the subtle ordering bug. :thumbsup:
Cody: one more note — add metric in the console for token-boundary-entropy spikes so future regressions more visible. small dashboard todo.
Ben: agreed. added ticket: https://tracker/redwood/ML-9933
Anya: closing loop: I'll update the eval ticket with repro, PR, rollback, and follow-ups. ping if I missed anything.
